Use this pathway after the normal electronics teaching and problem set. The notebooks support the circuit model; they do not replace deriving equations, building safely, or measuring a real system.

::: {.callout-note title="Current class position"}
Basic schematics and the five KCL/KVL questions are complete. The current bridge is **handwritten circuit equations → working Jupyter model → documentation-driven debugging → independent verification**. Capacitors and RC response follow this bridge.
:::

1. [Start with Python and JupyterLite](jupyterlite.qmd): run a cell, edit working code, preserve the notebook, and learn the browser workflow.
2. [Run Python and Jupyter on your own computer](local-python-jupyter.qmd): use a virtual environment in WSL, native Windows, macOS, or Linux instead of depending on JupyterLite.
3. [Find documentation and ask for programming help](finding-documentation-and-asking-for-help.qmd): reproduce an issue, search Python, NumPy, pandas, and Stack Overflow, and write a complete technical help request.
4. [Complete the Kirchhoff Jupyter assignment](kirchhoff-jupyter-assignment.qmd): verify one finished two-loop solution, document one repair, check residuals, and investigate a parameter change.
5. [Work through the Jupyter Electronics Lab](jupyter-electronics-lab.qmd): apply the skills across KCL/KVL, graphs, data, investigation, RC, op-amps, and the calculus bridge.
6. Continue to [Python measurement logging](../linux-operating-systems/python-data-logging.qmd) and [analysis and curve fitting](../linux-operating-systems/python-analysis-curve-fitting.qmd) when the investigation needs repeated measurements or a fitted model.

::: {.callout-important title="Current assignment"}
Open [Assignment: Verify Kirchhoff Equations with Jupyter](kirchhoff-jupyter-assignment.qmd). The assignment page contains the notebook download, setup choices, Tuesday instructions, required debugging evidence, submission checklist, assessment evidence, and the later work that is **not** due yet.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Core workflow"}
**Understand → Calculate → Build → Simulate → Measure → Verify → Investigate → Document → Share**

Most introductory notebook activities take about 15–30 minutes after the electronics calculation is complete. The [Jupyter Electronics Lab](jupyter-electronics-lab.qmd) also defines multi-day investigations that can carry the electronics course while students wait for components, instruments, or soldered kits.
:::

The browser route does not require a local installation or a new account, but the school browser must allow JupyterLite and WebAssembly. Download work before leaving the browser.

Hardware remains valuable, but it is not assumed to be simultaneously available to every student. A simulation-first submission is complete when it meets the stated modelling outcomes and labels its evidence honestly. Measurements can be added later as a separate validation stage.
